'''Alwyn Crendall Cashe''' (July 13, 1970 – November 8, 2005) was a [[United States Army]] [[non-commissioned officer|senior non-commissioned officer]] who was posthumously awarded the [[Medal of Honor]] for [[Hero|heroism]] in [[Iraq]]. On November 10, 2020, the [[United States Congress]] voted to upgrade Cashe's initially awarded [[Silver Star]] to the Medal of Honor. On December 16, 2021, more than 16 years after his death at age 35, Cashe's widow, Tamara,  accepted the Medal of Honor from President [[Joe Biden]] at a ceremony commemorating the actions of Cashe and two fellow soldiers for their acts in separate battles.<ref name="cashe">{{Cite web |last=Wentling |first=Nikki |date=16 December 2021 |title=Medals of Honor to be presented Thursday to three US soldiers |url=https://www.stripes.com/theaters/us/2021-12-15/medal-of-honor-soldiers-white-house-biden-3985824.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216025225/https://www.stripes.com/theaters/us/2021-12-15/medal-of-honor-soldiers-white-house-biden-3985824.html |archive-date=16 December 2021 |access-date=2022-08-03 |website=[[Stars and Stripes (newspaper)|Stars and Stripes]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="3rdIDmemoir">{{Cite web |last=Naylor |first=Justin A. |date=13 December 2021 |title=A Dogface Soldier through and through: Memories of SFC Alwyn Cashe |url=https://www.army.mil/article/252709/a_dogface_soldier_through_and_through_memories_of_sfc_alwyn_cashe?from=moh_cashe_news_text |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211217142551/https://www.army.mil/article/252709/a_dogface_soldier_through_and_through_memories_of_sfc_alwyn_cashe?from=moh_cashe_news_text |archive-date=17 December 2021 |website=Army.mil}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Cashe was born in [[Sanford, Florida]], on July 13, 1970.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-05-11 |title=Rep. Murphy Speech at Dedication Ceremony Honoring SFC Alwyn Cashe |url=https://murphy.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=1051 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220625203403/https://murphy.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=1051 |archive-date=25 June 2022 |access-date=2020-06-10 |website=U.S. Representative [[Stephanie Murphy]] |language=en}}</ref>  He was raised in [[Oviedo, Florida]], and attended [[Oviedo High School]], graduating in 1988.

==Military career==
Cashe enlisted in the [[United States Army]] following high school graduation in 1988.<ref name="thefallen">{{Cite web |title=Army Sgt. 1st Class Alwyn C. Cashe |url=https://thefallen.militarytimes.com/army-sgt-1st-class-alwyn-c-cashe/1302913 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220801190301/https://thefallen.militarytimes.com/army-sgt-1st-class-alwyn-c-cashe/1302913 |archive-date=1 August 2022 |access-date=2022-08-03 |website=The Fallen at [[Military Times]]}}</ref>  As an [[Infantry|infantryman]], he deployed in support of the [[Gulf War|1991 Gulf War]]. He also deployed to the former [[Yugoslavia]], earning the [[Kosovo Campaign Medal]]. Prior to his assignment to [[3rd Infantry Division (United States)|3rd Infantry Division]],<ref name="thefallen" /> he deployed once again to Iraq in support of [[Iraq War|Operation Iraqi Freedom]] following the [[2003 invasion of Iraq|2003 invasion]]. 

During his time in service he also served as a [[Drill instructor|drill sergeant]].

On the evening of October 17, 2005, Cashe, a member of A Company, 1st Battalion, [[15th Infantry Regiment (United States)|15th Infantry Regiment]], [[3rd Infantry Division (United States)|3rd Infantry Division]], saved the lives of six of his fellow soldiers after the [[Bradley fighting vehicle]] they were riding in struck an [[improvised explosive device]] despite suffering second and third-degree burns over 72% of his body.  Cashe succumbed to his injuries on November 8, 2005, at [[Brooke Army Medical Center]], [[Fort Sam Houston]], Texas.<ref name="valor">{{Cite web |title=Alwyn Crendall Cashe |url=http://valor.militarytimes.com/hero/29028 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220201211047/https://valor.militarytimes.com/hero/29028 |archive-date=1 February 2022 |access-date=2022-08-03 |website=Valor at [[Military Times]] |language=en}}</ref> Cashe is interred at Restlawn Cemetery in Sanford, Florida.

==Legacy==
On July 19, 2014, a new [[U.S. Army Reserve]] Center in Sanford, Florida was named in Cashe's honor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-07-19 |title=Army Reserve center dedicated to fallen Florida hero |url=https://www.dvidshub.net/news/136979/army-reserve-center-dedicated-fallen-florida-hero |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190617111515/https://www.dvidshub.net/news/136979/army-reserve-center-dedicated-fallen-florida-hero |archive-date=2019-06-17 |access-date=2020-09-02 |website=[[Defense Visual Information Distribution Service|DVIDS]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
On May 11, 2019, the Oviedo Post Office was renamed in Cashe's honor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Office of Rep. Stephanie Murphy |date=2019-05-09 |title=Murphy hosts post office dedication for Oviedo war hero |url=https://theseminolesource.com/murphy-hosts-post-office-dedication-oviedo-war-hero/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126132138/https://theseminolesource.com/murphy-hosts-post-office-dedication-oviedo-war-hero/ |archive-date=2020-11-26 |access-date=2020-06-10 |website=The Seminole Source |language=en-US}}</ref>

On July 23, 2020, Alwyn Cashe's son, Andrew Cashe, graduated [[One Station Unit Training]] (OSUT) for Infantry soldiers at [[Fort Benning|Fort Moore]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Packman |first=Aaron |date=2020-06-04 |title=SFC Alwyn Cashe's Son - Andrew, is half-way through Basic Combat Training |url=https://militaryvanguard.com/sfc-alwyn-cashes-sole-surviving-son-andrew-is-half-way-through-basic-combat-training/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200610193537/https://militaryvanguard.com/sfc-alwyn-cashes-sole-surviving-son-andrew-is-half-way-through-basic-combat-training/ |archive-date=2020-06-10 |access-date=2020-06-10 |website=Military Vanguard |language=en-US}}</ref>

On May 20, 2021, [[3rd Infantry Division (United States)|3rd Infantry Division]] at [[Fort Stewart|Fort Stewart, GA]] renamed their primary ceremonial grounds from “Marne Gardens” to “Cashe Gardens”. Located next to the Division Headquarters, Cashe Gardens is utilized by the installation for Battalion, Brigade, and Division Changes of Command as well as other high-profile ceremonies.<ref name="stewwart">{{Cite web |last=Beynon |first=Steve |date=2021-05-19 |title=Fort Stewart to Honor Iraq War Hero Alwyn Cashe as Medal of Honor Remains in Limbo |url=https://www.military.com/daily-news/2021/05/19/fort-stewart-honor-iraq-war-hero-alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor-remains-limbo.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220601120749/https://www.military.com/daily-news/2021/05/19/fort-stewart-honor-iraq-war-hero-alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor-remains-limbo.html |archive-date=2022-06-01 |access-date=2021-07-09 |publisher=[[Military.com]]}}</ref>

===Campaign to upgrade Cashe's Silver Star to the Medal of Honor===
[[Gary Brito]], Cashe's battalion commander at the time of the action, did not initially realize the extent of Cashe's injuries and the pain he must have been in when he nominated Cashe for the Silver Star award.  Witnesses were evacuated for medical treatment and unavailable for statement.  Brito subsequently submitted additional statements to the Army to justify upgrading Cashe's award to the Medal of Honor.  Brito continued to support efforts to upgrade Cashe's Silver Star to the Medal of Honor<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zucchino |first=David |date=2014-12-07 |title=Medal of Honor campaign continues for black sergeant who saved troops |url=https://www.latimes.com/nation/la-na-medal-of-honor-20141207-story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220105025359/https://www.latimes.com/nation/la-na-medal-of-honor-20141207-story.html |archive-date=2022-01-05 |access-date=2020-06-10 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

On October 17, 2019, the 14th anniversary of Cashe's actions, three members of Congress wrote<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-17 |title=Murphy, Crenshaw, Waltz Urge the Defense Department to Award Alwyn Cashe the Medal of Honor |url=https://murphy.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=1134 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220625203340/https://murphy.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=1134 |archive-date=2022-06-25 |access-date=2020-06-10 |website=U.S. Representative Stephanie Murphy |language=en}}</ref> to Defense Secretary [[Mark Esper]] and Army Secretary [[Ryan D. McCarthy|Ryan McCarthy]] formally requesting an upgrade of Cashe's award to the Medal of Honor.  The letter was authored by retired Navy SEAL [[Dan Crenshaw]], former Special Forces officer [[Michael Waltz]], and [[Stephanie Murphy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harkins |first=Gina |date=2019-10-17 |title=Vets in Congress Renew Medal of Honor Plea for Army 'Legend' Alwyn Cashe |url=https://www.military.com/daily-news/2019/10/17/vets-congress-renew-medal-honor-plea-army-legend-alwyn-cashe.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210316065518/https://www.military.com/daily-news/2019/10/17/vets-congress-renew-medal-honor-plea-army-legend-alwyn-cashe.html |archive-date=2021-03-16 |access-date=2020-06-10 |website=[[Military.com]] |language=en}}</ref>

On August 24, 2020, Secretary of Defense, [[Mark Esper]], agreed that Cashe's actions merited award of the Medal of Honor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shane III |first=Leo |date=2020-08-30 |title=Iraq War hero Alwyn Cashe should get Medal of Honor, Esper says |url=https://www.militarytimes.com/news/pentagon-congress/2020/08/28/esper-says-he-will-back-medal-of-honor-for-iraq-war-hero-alwyn-cashe/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220609045448/https://www.militarytimes.com/news/pentagon-congress/2020/08/28/esper-says-he-will-back-medal-of-honor-for-iraq-war-hero-alwyn-cashe/ |archive-date=2022-06-09 |access-date=2020-09-30 |website=[[Military Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
On September 22, 2020, the U.S. House of Representatives unanimously passed a bill, introduced by Rep. Stephanie Murphy (D-FL), which allowed Cashe to finally receive the Medal of Honor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thayer |first=Rose L. |date=2020-09-23 |title=House passes bill to clear path for Army Sgt. 1st Class Alwyn Cashe to receive posthumous Medal of Honor |url=https://www.stripes.com/news/us/house-passes-bill-to-clear-path-for-army-sgt-1st-class-alwyn-cashe-to-receive-posthumous-medal-of-honor-1.646115?fbclid=IwAR20KyqnR-v5zLhtBvXk089c33DEh-tQMEIt5gRRVwuDN1Tk6-NnB3aUTuI |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220803202427/https://www.stripes.com/theaters/us/house-passes-bill-to-clear-path-for-army-sgt-1st-class-alwyn-cashe-to-receive-posthumous-medal-of-honor-1.646115 |archive-date=2022-08-03 |access-date=2020-09-30 |website=[[Stars and Stripes (newspaper)|Stars and Stripes]]}}</ref>  HR 8276 waived a five-year time statute of limitations that expired for normal consideration for Medal of Honor awards by directly authorizing the President to award the medal “for acts of valor during Operation Iraqi Freedom.”<ref>{{Cite web |last=Powers |first=Scott |date=2020-09-23 |title=House passes Stephanie Murphy bill making Medal of Honor possible for Alwyn Cashe |url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/369038-house-passes-stephanie-murphy-bill-making-medal-of-honor-possible-for-alwyn-cashe |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220124322/https://floridapolitics.com/archives/369038-house-passes-stephanie-murphy-bill-making-medal-of-honor-possible-for-alwyn-cashe/ |archive-date=2021-12-20 |access-date=2020-09-30 |website=Florida Politics |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[File:SFC Alwyn C. Cashe is Posthumously Awarded the Medal of Honor by President Biden 211216-A-VS818-372.jpg|thumb|Cashe's wife Tamara accepts the Medal of Honor on her husband's behalf during a ceremony at the [[White House]] on December 16, 2021.]]

On September 28, 2020, [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] left tackle [[Alejandro Villanueva (American football)|Alejandro Villanueva]], a former US Army ranger, taped Cashe's name on the back of his helmet, covering the name of [[Shooting of Antwon Rose Jr.|Antwon Rose Jr]], who was killed by an East Pittsburgh policeman in June 2018. The team had previously decided to honor Rose.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guggenheimer |first=Paul |date=2020-09-16 |title=Who is Alwyn Cashe and why did Alejandro Villanueva choose to honor him? |url=https://triblive.com/sports/steelers/who-is-alwyn-cashe-and-why-did-alejandro-villanueva-choose-to-honor-him/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210110233449/https://triblive.com/sports/steelers/who-is-alwyn-cashe-and-why-did-alejandro-villanueva-choose-to-honor-him/ |archive-date=2021-01-10 |access-date=2020-09-30 |website=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]}}</ref>  Villanueva stated his actions were intended to support the campaign to award Cashe the Medal of Honor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Popejoy |first=Curt |date=2020-09-28 |title=Steelers OT Alejandro Villanueva finally clears air about his helmet |url=https://steelerswire.usatoday.com/2020/09/28/steelers-alejandro-villanueva-alwyn-cashe-helmet-antwon-rose/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210801125904/https://steelerswire.usatoday.com/2020/09/28/steelers-alejandro-villanueva-alwyn-cashe-helmet-antwon-rose/ |archive-date=2021-08-01 |access-date=2020-09-30 |website=Steelers Wire |language=en-US}}</ref>

On November 10, 2020, the Senate passed legislation that cleared the way for Cashe to be awarded the Medal of Honor.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lamothe |first=Dan |date=10 November 2020 |title=Iraq War soldier Alwyn Cashe set to receive Medal of Honor after Senate passage of legislation |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2020/11/10/iraq-war-soldier-alwyn-cashe-set-receive-medal-honor-after-senate-passage-legislation/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120061740/https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2020/11/10/iraq-war-soldier-alwyn-cashe-set-receive-medal-honor-after-senate-passage-legislation/ |archive-date=20 November 2020 |access-date=10 November 2020 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref>

On December 4, 2020, President [[Donald Trump]] signed [https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/house-bill/8276 H.R. 8276], which authorized the President to posthumously award the Medal of Honor to Alwyn C. Cashe.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=David |date=5 December 2020 |title=Iraq War hero Alwyn Cashe is closer to being awarded the Medal of Honor |url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/05/politics/alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor-law-trnd/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216212116/https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/05/politics/alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor-law-trnd/index.html |archive-date=16 December 2021 |access-date=9 January 2021 |publisher=[[CNN]]}}</ref>

===Awarding of the Medal of Honor===
It was hoped by members of Cashe's family and several U.S. House Representatives that the award ceremony would take place as fast as possible.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seck |first=Hope Hodge |date=5 January 2021  |title=Alwyn Cashe's Medal of Honor Package Is Headed to the White House, Family Says |url=https://www.military.com/daily-news/2021/01/05/alwyn-cashes-medal-of-honor-package-headed-white-house-family-says.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210408214943/https://www.military.com/daily-news/2021/01/05/alwyn-cashes-medal-of-honor-package-headed-white-house-family-says.html |archive-date=8 April 2021 |access-date=21 February 2021 |publisher=[[Military.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Britzky |first=Haley |date=6 January 2021 |title=Trump poised to award Medal of Honor to Alwyn Cashe, 15 years after he gave his life to save his men |url=https://taskandpurpose.com/news/alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor-pentagon-endorsement/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805074316/https://taskandpurpose.com/news/alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor-pentagon-endorsement/ |archive-date=5 August 2021 |access-date=21 February 2021 |publisher=[[Task & Purpose]]}}</ref> However, on January 11, 2021, it was announced that it was now expected to happen after President Biden assumed office on January 20.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Britzky |first=Haley |date=11 January 2021 |title=White House postpones Medal of Honor for Alwyn Cashe until after the inauguration |url=https://taskandpurpose.com/news/alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor-delayed-white-house/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220803203622/https://taskandpurpose.com/military-life/alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor-delayed-white-house/ |archive-date=3 August 2022 |access-date=21 February 2021 |publisher=[[Task & Purpose]]}}</ref>
President Biden awarded three Medals of Honor, to Cashe's family, [[Earl Plumlee]] and the family of [[Christopher Celiz]], in a ceremony on December 16, 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lamothe |first=Dan |date=15 December 2021 |title=After extraordinary sacrifice — and years of delay — Alwyn Cashe gets his Medal of Honor |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2021/12/15/alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211215111117/https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2021/12/15/alwyn-cashe-medal-of-honor/ |archive-date=15 December 2021 |access-date=16 December 2021 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Deena |first1=Zaru |last2=Robinson |first2=Adia |date=16 December 2021 |title=Alwyn Cashe set to become first Black recipient of Medal of Honor for service in post-9/11 war on terror |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/alwyn-cashe-set-black-recipient-medal-honor-service/story?id=81769891 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220720173129/https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/alwyn-cashe-set-black-recipient-medal-honor-service/story?id=81769891 |archive-date=20 July 2022 |access-date=16 December 2021 |publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]}}</ref>

==Awards and decorations==
===Silver Star===
{{quotebox|[[File:Silver Star medal.png|70px|center]]
{{center|<big>'''Alwyn Crendall Cashe'''</big>}}
{{center|Rank and organization: Sergeant First Class, U.S. Army, Company A, 1st Battalion, 15th Infantry Regiment, 3rd Infantry Division}}
{{center|Place and date: Iraq, 17 October 2005}}
{{center|Awarded for actions during: Global War on Terror}}
{{center|Born: July 13, 1970, Thompson, Georgia}}

'''Citation:'''

<blockquote>The President of the United States of America, authorized by Act of Congress July 9, 1918 (amended by an act of July 25, 1963), takes pride in presenting the Silver Star (Posthumously) to Sergeant First Class Alwyn Crendall Cashe, United States Army, for exceptionally valorous achievement following an improvised explosive device explosion on 17 October 2005, while serving with Company A, 1st Battalion, 15th Infantry Regiment, 3d Infantry Division, during combat operations in support of Operation IRAQI FREEDOM. Sergeant First Class Cashe's disregard for his own safety proved evident when he saved the lives of six fellow soldiers despite his serious injuries. His bravery is in keeping with the finest traditions of military heroism and reflect distinct credit upon himself, Task Force DRAGON, the SLEDGEHAMMER Brigade, Task Force LIBERTY, and the United States Army. NARRATIVE TO ACCOMPANY AWARD: Sergeant First Class Alwyn Crendall Cashe heroically distinguished himself by exceptionally valorous conduct in the face of the enemy of the United States as a Platoon Sergeant in 1st Platoon, Alpha Company (HARDOCK), 1st Battalion, 15th Infantry Regiment stationed at Forward Operating Base MACKENZIE, Iraq, on 17 October 2005. On the evening of 17 October 2005, Sergeant First Class Cashe's heroic actions saved the lives of six of his fellow soldiers. At approximately 1920 hours, 1st Platoon of Alpha Company, 1-15 Infantry departed FOB MACKENZIE to conduct a route clearance in the city of Daliaya, Iraq. Along Route JAIME, the lead Bradley Fighting Vehicle, of which Sergeant First Class Cashe was gunner having just moved from a NMC vehicle, struck a victim detonated pressure-switch IED at grid MC 25357243. The blast ignited the fuel cell on the vehicle causing fuel to spew everywhere. The vehicle came to a stop and immediately erupted in flames. Sergeant First Class Cashe was initially slightly injured and drenched with fuel. Despite his condition, he bravely managed to get out of the gunner's hatch, crawl down the BFV and assist the driver out of the driver's hatch. The driver had been burned and Sergeant First Class Cashe extinguished his flames. The following minutes were crucial. Six soldiers and a translator were in the back of the Bradley. Flames had engulfed the entire vehicle from the bottom and were coming out of every portal. The squad leader inside the vehicle managed to open the troop hatch door to help the soldiers escape. Without regard for his personal safety, Sergeant First Class Cashe rushed to the back of the vehicle, reaching into the hot flames and started pulling out his soldiers. The flames gripped his fuel soaked uniform. Flames quickly spread all over his body. Despite the terrible pain, Sergeant First Class Cashe placed the injured soldier on the ground and returned to the burning vehicle to retrieve another burning soldier; all the while, he was still on fire. A crew from a trail Bradley arrived within moments and assisted with CASEVAC. During all this and with severe burns, Sergeant First Class Cashe bravely continued to take control of the chaos. Within minutes, the company First Sergeant was on the scene and began to evacuate the seriously injured soldiers. One of which was Sergeant First Class Cashe. In the end, the national translator was killed in action, and 10 soldiers were injured. Seven of the ten were very seriously injured. Sergeant First Class Cashe stayed a hero through it all. His injuries were the worst as he suffered from 2d and 3d degree burns over 72% of his body. Sergeant First Class Cashe's heroic actions saved the lives of six of his beloved soldiers. He is truly deserving of this award. His actions are in keeping with the finest traditions of military heroism and reflect distinct credit upon himself, Task Force LIBERTY and the United States Army.<ref name="valor"/></blockquote> }}

{{Clear}}

===Medal of Honor===
{{quotebox|[[File:Moh army mil.jpg|130px|center]]
{{center|<big>'''Alwyn Crendall Cashe'''</big>}}
{{center|Rank and organization: Sergeant First Class, U.S. Army, Company A, 1st Battalion, 15th Infantry Regiment, 3rd Infantry Division}}
{{center|Place and date: Salah Ad Din Province, Iraq, 17 October 2005}}
{{center|Awarded for actions during: Global War on Terror}}
{{center|Born: July 13, 1970, Thompson, Georgia}}

'''Citation:'''

<blockquote>The President of the United States of America, authorized by Act of Congress March 3rd, 1863, has posthumously awarded in the name of Congress the Medal of Honor to Sergeant First Class Alwyn C. Cashe, United States Army, for conspicuous gallantry at the risk of his life above and beyond the call of duty. Sergeant First Class Alwyn C. Cashe distinguished himself by acts of gallantry above and beyond the call of duty while serving as Platoon Sergeant with Company A, 1st Battalion, 15th Infantry Regiment, 3rd Brigade, 3rd Infantry Division in Salah Ad Din Province, Iraq, on October 17th, 2005. While on a nighttime mounted patrol near an enemy-laden village, the Bradley Fighting Vehicle which Sergeant First Class Cashe was commanding was attacked by enemy small-arms fire and an improvised explosive device, which disabled the vehicle and engulfed it in flames. After extracting himself from the vehicle, Sergeant First Class Cashe set about extracting the driver, who was trapped in the vehicle. After opening the driver’s hatch, Sergeant First Class Cashe and a fellow soldier extracted the driver, who was engulfed in the flames. During the course of extinguishing the flames on the driver and extracting him from the vehicle, Sergeant First Class Cashe’s fuel soaked his uniform, igniting and causing severe burns to his body. Ignoring his painful wounds, Sergeant First Class Cashe then moved to the rear of the vehicle to continue in aiding his fellow soldiers who were trapped in the troop compartment. At this time, the enemy noted his movements and began to direct their fire on his position. When another element of the company engaged the enemy, Sergeant First Class Cashe seized the opportunity and moved into the open troop door and aided four of his soldiers in escaping the burning vehicle. Having extracted the four soldiers, Sergeant First Class Cashe noticed two other soldiers had not been accounted for and again he entered the building [sic] to retrieve them. At this time, reinforcements arrived to further suppress the enemy and establish a Casualty Collection Point. Despite the severe second- and third-degree burns covering the majority of his body, Sergeant First Class Cashe persevered through the pain to encourage his fellow soldiers and ensure they received needed medical care. When medical evacuation helicopters began to arrive, Sergeant First Class Cashe selflessly refused evacuation until all of the other wounded soldiers were evacuated first. Sergeant First Class Cashe’s extraordinary heroism and selflessness above and beyond the call of duty were keeping with the highest traditions of the military service and reflect great credit upon himself, his unit, and the United States Army. {{center|Signed<br> <big>'''Joseph R. Biden'''</big> <br>the President of the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 December 2021 |title=Remarks by President Biden at Presentation of the Medal of Honor |url=https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/speeches-remarks/2021/12/16/remarks-by-president-biden-at-presentation-of-the-medal-of-honor/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220707004419/https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/speeches-remarks/2021/12/16/remarks-by-president-biden-at-presentation-of-the-medal-of-honor/ |archive-date=7 July 2022 |access-date=19 December 2021 |url-status=live |website=[[White House]]}}</ref>}}</blockquote> }}

{{Clear}}
